title: Colts name QB Anthony Richardson Sr. top backup behind starter Daniel Jones
content:
Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen announced Thursday that Anthony Richardson Sr. will be the team’s top backup quarterback. Richardson, the Colts’ first-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, competed with 2025 sixth-round pick Riley Leonard throughout training camp to serve as QB2 behind starter Daniel Jones.

Early on, it seemed as if Leonard had the edge in the competition, but Richardson’s superior play in the preseason seems to have won him the job.

Richardson completed 21 of 33 passes for 249 yards with zero touchdowns and one interception in three preseason games. He also had 10 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown and lost one fumble while running. Leonard, meanwhile, completed 20 of 42 passes for 199 yards, zero touchdowns and two picks. He added six carries for 17 yards and fumbled two snaps, though neither was lost.

Richardson winning the top backup job for the Colts is the latest turn of what has been a roller coaster career with Indianapolis. Just in the past year or so alone, Richardson lost his starting job to Jones, then nearly lost an eye after breaking his orbital bone in a freak pregame accident last season. Then, to start the offseason, Richardson formally requested a trade. The 24-year-old was seemingly looking for a fresh start in a new NFL city. However, no trade materialized, with GM Chris Ballard saying in late July that Indianapolis was not going to “give him away.”

Richardson’s trade request remained intact throughout training camp and the preseason, but assistant GM Ed Dodds strongly hinted in mid-August that the Colts were intending to keep Richardson.

“I think you take care of your own team first,” Dodds said. “We want to have three (quarterbacks) who can play. So, if (Richardson) is one of them, he’s going to be here.”

A few weeks later, Ballard said he fully expected Richardson to remain with the team this year.

“I’ve been pretty consistent with Anthony,” Ballard said Monday, three days before Steichen named Richardson the top backup. “We forget how young he is sometimes. Really proud of his growth. … There were two times in camp that I said, ‘OK, he’s starting to really show some poise.’ The two-minute against New England — remember, we’re backed up. I think it was 38 seconds left on the clock, (and he) gets us in field goal range to give us a chance to get points. And then during the Atlanta scrimmage, he had a tremendous two-minute drill also, so it’s been fun to watch Anthony’s growth.”

In other Colts news, the team announced five team captains: Jones, left guard Quenton Nelson, running back Jonathan Taylor, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and safety Cam Bynum. Jones has been a captain eight times in his career, including last year with the Colts.

Buckner is also an eight-time captain, including the past six consecutive seasons with Indianapolis. Nelson, too, has been a captain for six consecutive seasons in Indy. Meanwhile, Taylor will be a Colts captain for the third time in his career, and Bynum will be a captain for the first time.
